version.changelog:
- Skill renamed from "crypto-market-data" to "crypto-market-data-aisa" for clarity.
- Improved descriptions to clarify AIsa integration and primary use cases.
- Terminology and phrasing streamlined throughout documentation; focus on crypto research, token lookup, and market data workflows.
- Inputs, outputs, and feature summaries made more concise for easier reading.
- Minor corrections to requirements and usage notes.

llm.summary: The skill is a mostly read-only crypto market data client, but its top-level routing text overclaims support for stock and dividend work that the code does not provide.

dimensions.detail: Network access to https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1 and the AISA_API_KEY environment variable are disclosed and proportionate for authenticated crypto market data queries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains a markdown skill file, README, and one Python CLI script; no installer, dependency installation, hook, or automatic execution mechanism was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The body later says not to use the skill for equities or traditional finance data, creating a concrete contradiction with the top-level activation text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background worker, local credential-store access, file mutation, privilege escalation, or destructive behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bundled Python client only implements authenticated GET requests to AIsa CoinGecko cryptocurrency endpoints, while the manifest and README also advertise stock analysis and dividend research.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a CoinGecko-through-AIsa cryptocurrency data CLI. Do not rely on this skill for stocks, dividends, or traditional finance despite the top-level wording, and keep the AISA_API_KEY out of committed files or shared logs.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Supported by artifact evidence: top-level metadata advertises unsupported stock and dividend use cases even though the script is crypto-only.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported for the README/SKILL mismatch: stock and dividend claims are not backed by implemented endpoints.
[LP3] expected: Downgraded in context: env-key and network use are disclosed and necessary for the stated AIsa API client, though explicit permission scoping would improve reviewability.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Supported: broad financial activation language can route non-crypto requests to this crypto-only skill.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported: the skill says both to use it for stock/dividend workflows and not to use it for equities or traditional finance.
[E1] expected: Downgraded in context: the external transmission is the documented API call path and sends the required bearer API key to the declared AIsa endpoint.
[SQP-2] expected: Minor documentation issue: secret-handling caution is sparse, but the required AISA_API_KEY is disclosed in the skill metadata and requirements.
